record.original_question: Under what physical conditions can a pulsar plasma supply not only the charge density required by electrodynamic models but also the required current density, and when does current starvation occur instead? More specifically, when the plasma cannot supply the required cross-field current needed to maintain the time-dependent corotation charge density, how should the resulting departure from corotation and the associated regions with nonzero parallel electric field be modeled in a self-consistent way?

evidence.quote: Any model for pulsar electrodynamics can be valid only if the plasma is able to supply not only the required charge density, but also the required current density.

When this condition is not satisfied, there is current starvation, and (ω × x)⊥ cannot be maintained at its required instantaneous value. Corotation, even in the restricted sense implied by vcor⊥ , cf. (2.9), is then not possible and the RMM is invalid.
Second, inclusion of Jdisp , in a corotation model, leads to the inevitability of current starvation, §4.6, with possibly important implications.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a rotating, magnetized neutron star (a pulsar) with angular velocity vector ω, and let B(x,t) and E(x,t) denote the electromagnetic fields in its magnetosphere, sourced together with a plasma of charged particles (electrons, positrons, ions). In ideal corotation, the plasma drifts with the perpendicular corotation velocity v_cor⊥ = (ω × x)⊥, the charge density takes the Goldreich–Julian value ρ_GJ = −ε₀ ∇·(v_cor × B), and a particular current density J_req (including a displacement contribution J_disp = ε₀ ∂E/∂t arising from time dependence in an obliquely rotating frame) is required to maintain this configuration self-consistently with Maxwell's equations.

(a) Identify the physical conditions on the local plasma (number densities, available charge carriers, mobility along and across B, pair-creation supply, etc.) under which the magnetospheric plasma is able to supply simultaneously both the required charge density ρ_GJ and the required current density J_req everywhere in the magnetosphere.

(b) Characterize the regime of "current starvation," in which the plasma cannot supply the cross-field component of J_req needed to sustain the time-dependent corotation charge density, and determine where in the magnetosphere this regime is unavoidable.

(c) In regions where current starvation occurs, develop a self-consistent model describing (i) the resulting departure of the plasma flow from corotation v_cor⊥, and (ii) the appearance and structure of regions ("gaps") supporting a nonzero parallel electric field E_∥ = (E·B)/|B|, including its back-reaction on the particle motion, pair production, and the global magnetospheric current circuit.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of a self-consistent treatment of current starvation and parallel-electric-field gaps in pulsar magnetospheres remains open. Recent PIC and Vlasov simulations (e.g., 2024 limit-cycle pair-production models, 2025 1D Vlasov QED-cascade simulations over polar caps) explore aspects of gap dynamics and screening but do not provide a complete global self-consistent analytic model; current starvation continues to be discussed as an unresolved feature of pulsar electrodynamics.

status_evidence.title: A Model for Pair Production Limit Cycles in Pulsar Magnetospheres
status_evidence.snippet: Screening of the parallel electric field by pair cascade manifests as a limit cycle, as E_∥ is recurrently induced when pairs escape from the gap region.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work treats E_∥ screening dynamically but only as a local limit cycle, not a global self-consistent solution.

status_evidence.title: 1D Vlasov Simulations of QED Cascades Over Pulsar Polar Caps
status_evidence.snippet: Vlasov simulations of polar-cap cascades exploring gap formation and screening.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025, gap and current-supply problems are still being studied with kinetic simulations rather than resolved analytically.

status_evidence.title: Pulsar Electrodynamics: an unsolved problem
status_evidence.snippet: A form of current starvation occurs, implying a new class of gaps.
status_evidence.claim: The need for a self-consistent model of current starvation is articulated as still unresolved.
